outcome.technical: PART 2 (blocks as the sweep's unit). tools/sweep-selftests.py: stage_labels() reads a staged suite's STAGES literal off the AST (None for computed, empty, misshapen, nested or duplicate-label tables); staged_blocks() maps path->labels; work_items() orders every job costliest-estimate first (a block = file cost / blocks; ties by path, then table order); sweep() runs each block as its own run_one child (--selftest --stage L --cases-to P, own scratch/home/git config, watched like a file, one slot from the same slot_gate in ticket order, timeout = file_timeout at stage_grant(jobs) slots, still cut by the deadline); the thread ending a suite's last block writes the block list and starts the suite once more with --selftest --replay LIST on the slot it holds; suite_ran() folds blocks+replay into one row (replay's exit/output, block debris prefixed 'block L,' and dropped for a killed block, summed seconds as slot-seconds, grant 1, blocks N, one window per process); claude_verdicts() accepts a list of windows; timing() prints '[Ns, N blocks]' and costs_from_render reads it unmultiplied; budget_line() appends which staged suites run block by block and how many blocks. A staged suite whose table cannot be read still runs whole on a grant (bg5/bg6/tt0 fixtures keep that path). --shard is untouched: blocks follow their file's part; record_costs keeps per-file slot-seconds. tests/_harness.py: block_result() is the one reading of a block for both runners (run_stage now calls it; messages unchanged except 'exit %s'); replay_results() split out of run_stages(); replayed() + replay_selftest() + staged_main '--replay PATH': STAGES order, a missing label is ONE failing 'DID NOT REPORT' case, a stray label a failing 'RAN BUT IS NOT STAGED' case, an unreadable list 'REPLAY READ NOTHING', then stage_faults and label_faults as a full run. PART 1 (less work in tests/test_drive_phase.py): _drive_follower_map copied all of plugins/audit/scripts into the fixture (committed, checked out per task tree) so its _deps.py --write-map read the whole plugin (about 5 s CPU per run, two runs per drive, three drives: fm, fi and al's re-run of fm); it now copies _output.py only. Process-seconds of the suite's 114 blocks (wait4 rusage incl. children, 6 at a time, machine shared, load avg 18-20 on 10 cores), two pairs about an hour apart: before 1156.7 / 1098.0, after 1097.2 / 1053.8; the three targeted blocks fell 40.2 / 35.3 (fm 20.05->7.68, fi 20.51->8.04, al 58.81->43.44), the other 111 moved -19.3 / -8.8, which is load noise. ALSO FOUND AND FIXED: per-block watched scratch exposed that every writer/reviewer session the suite plays left run-agent-session.py's session-writer-*/session-reviewer-* TMPDIR in the block's temp dir (13 blocks; the old per-block TMPDIR under fixture_root was removed at exit and hid it); _play_session now hands the session a fixture_root temp dir. The other seven staged suites were run block by block through the sweep's own run_one: every block exit 0, every case passing, no debris. CASE COUNTS (tally lines): test_drive_phase.py 574 -> 574 (HEAD blocks sum 574; after, both through the harness pool and through the sweep's block path 'ALL PASS: 574/574'); tools/sweep-selftests.py 128 -> 135 (bb1, bb1b, bb2-bb6 added; sb1 now asserts the replay line); tests/_harness.py 85 -> 89 (sr14-sr17 added; sr13 rewritten from 'pool sized by the grant' to 'blocks run as the sweep's jobs, replayed in STAGES order'). tests/test__harness.py was NOT created: _output_lints.selftest_coverage() reports a tests/test_*.py naming no module under scripts/ or hooks/ as an orphan (its docstring says tests/_harness.py is not an orphan candidate), so that file would turn the sweep red; the harness cases stay in tests/_harness.py's own selftest, which the sweep runs. COMMANDS: ruff check (3 files) exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0; prose_number_claims/house_style_violations over the tree: none in these files; own gate exit 0 ('1/1 files ok, 135 cases'). SIMULATION (not a measurement; scratchpad/p142-11/sim.py, list scheduling over .github/sweep-costs.json with drive_phase blocks from the measured shape): the block model reaches total/slots, the grant model sits above it (8 slots: 657 vs 627 table-seconds); with a local-like table of 2200 slot-s (drive_phase 1343) the block model is 275 s before and 266 s after this task's cut. So under the 240 s acceptance this task's work cut is not enough on its own: what remains is verb start-up (about 5400 Python processes per run of this suite; drive-phase.py and audit-task.py imports cost about 0.12-0.17 s CPU each) and the other suites. Declined lever: running submit in-process instead of as a command (about 50 s) - the suite's stated design is that the agent's last act is a command, and every drive exercises that path under the cp1252 leg. DEPENDANTS: tests/_harness.py importers (test__ado_* .. test__affected_tests and the rest) - still correct, run/check/fixture_root/run_stage/run_stages/stage_timeout/STAGE_TIMEOUT_MARGIN keep their signatures and behaviour (test_audit_task ps2/ps3 and test_drive_phase al-block use them; both re-run green); _group_present/_pid_present (test_run_test_gate), _labels (test__usage_viz), _load_sweep (test_drive_phase) unchanged. tests/test_drive_phase.py dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json - not edited, its per-file entry still means slot-seconds; drive-phase.py, test__runner_output.py, test_run_test_gate.py (_counting, _follower_cases, _head unchanged), tools/sweep-selftests.py (bg2b still finds it staged), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (_load unchanged), docs/research files - still correct. tools/sweep-selftests.py dependants: before-you-claim evals.json, _output.py, _filed_returns.py - path mentions, still correct; _runner_collects.py reads SWEEP_DIRS and _runner_output.py the FAIL lines - both unchanged; stamp-verification.py sweep_budget reads the cost table per file - unchanged meaning; sweep-costs.json format unchanged; budget_line named in _warning_groups.py is audit-status's own function, not this one; locale_decision (test_drive_phase) and named_suites (test_derive_phase_gate) unchanged; test_stamp_verification's _SWEEP_GREEN spells the old budget line as a stand-in fixture and is not compared with live output. SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT sizes its block pool' paragraph), CONTRIBUTING.md ('THE WORKERS ARE ONE BUDGET OF SLOTS' paragraph) and .github/workflows/ci.yml (comment above the sweep matrix) still describe the grant model; tests/test_integrate_task.py copies all of scripts/ into a fixture the same way (al-block re-runs that suite whole, about 21 s of its CPU is those write-maps).
